title: Establish the two-tier token system, app shell, self-hosted fonts, and pre-paint theme resolve
description: Lay the reskin foundation every later slice paints on. In public/styles.css build the ADR-001 two-tier tokens: a raw --c-* palette feeding a semantic role layer (--bg, --surface, --fg, --accent, --danger, --over-*, …) with a full dark set under [data-theme=dark] and a light set under [data-theme=light], plus a rem type scale (1.25 ratio, 12->40px) and a 4pt spacing scale, and the ordered per-category colour palette custom properties (ADR-001/ADR-005). Also add the base app-shell layout: a two-column grid (fixed 260px sidebar + fluid main), the sidebar chrome (brand mark, empty nav container, foot container), the main column (sticky blurred top bar holding the view title + the existing Add-expense button, a content wrap holding three empty view sections, footer), and the shared surface/card/panel/table primitives and system-font fallback stacks with font-display:swap. Rewrite public/index.html into that skeleton (keep loading app.js as a module; keep the Add-expense button element and its id wiring intact for existing handlers), self-host Inter + JetBrains Mono as .woff2 files under public/ referenced via @font-face, and add a single '.woff2':'font/woff2' entry to server.js's TYPES map. Add the ADR-002 inline synchronous <head> script that resolves the theme BEFORE first paint: use a saved localStorage['lb-theme'] if present, else matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'), and set data-theme on <html> immediately. Keep app.js booting and rendering the (still-present) three views into the new containers so the app stays functional.html.
acceptanceCriteria: With no saved choice and an OS dark preference, the document root gets data-theme="dark" and the page paints on the dark --bg without a post-load theme flip
With localStorage['lb-theme']='light' set before load, the root resolves to data-theme="light"
The layout is a two-column grid: a 260px-wide sidebar element and a fluid main column beside it
styles.css defines the semantic role tokens (--bg,--surface,--fg,--accent,--danger) under both [data-theme=dark] and [data-theme=light], and no downstream rule references a raw hex literal
server.js's TYPES map returns 'font/woff2' for a .woff2 request
Inter and JetBrains Mono are referenced via @font-face pointing at self-hosted public/*.woff2 files, not the Google Fonts CDN

The app shell reproduces attachment-01.html's frame: a fixed-width left sidebar column beside a fluid main column, a sticky top bar spanning the main column with the view title on the left and the Add-expense button on the right, and the dark palette's page background, surface and accent colours taken from that file's tokens
rationale: The token plumbing, the two-column shell, the self-hosted fonts, the server MIME entry, and the pre-paint theme resolve are the shared foundation every other slice builds on; isolating them keeps each later behavioural slice small and lets themes flip by a single attribute. It must land alone in its own wave because it rewrites index.html, seeds styles.css, and changes server.js that all siblings depend on.

title: Add the sun/moon theme toggle that flips and remembers the theme
description: Add the sun/moon icon button at the foot of the sidebar (beside a quiet 'signed in' line), matching the mockup. Clicking it flips the root data-theme dark<->light live and writes the chosen value to localStorage['lb-theme'] so the saved choice overrides the OS on subsequent loads until the next toggle. The correct sun/moon glyph shows for the active theme. Builds on the pre-paint resolve and token layer from t-001.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking the sidebar toggle when data-theme is 'dark' sets it to 'light' (and vice versa)
After a toggle, localStorage['lb-theme'] holds the newly chosen theme value
Reloading after a toggle re-applies the saved theme regardless of the OS preference
The toggle button sits inside the sidebar foot region

The theme toggle reproduces attachment-01.html's sidebar foot: an icon-only sun/moon button sitting on the same row as the quiet 'signed in' line, at the bottom of the sidebar, with the mockup's muted icon colour
rationale: The write side of theming (flip + persist) is a distinct user-observable behaviour from t-001's read-side resolve; splitting it keeps each theme slice cohesive and independently testable.

title: Add the sidebar nav with client-side view switching, active pill, and seed-derived badges
description: Populate the sidebar nav container from t-001 with the three vertical nav items (Expenses / Categories / Summary) each with its icon, matching the mockup. Clicking one switches the visible main content view client-side among the three existing views (show/hide), marks the active item with the emerald filled pill and aria-current=true, and updates the top-bar title to the active view's name. No routing library, no new store. Also render the mockup's nav badges derived from the seed at render time (NOT a live-tracking feature): an item-count badge on Expenses = expenses.length, and a red alert badge on Categories showing the over-budget category count, shown ONLY when that count > 0 (so absent with the current seed, which has none over budget). Presence-of-badge is the mockup's look; live counts stay out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: The sidebar shows exactly three nav items labelled Expenses, Categories, Summary
Clicking a nav item shows only that view's section and hides the other two
The clicked nav item gets aria-current="true" and the other two get aria-current="false"
The top-bar title text updates to match the active view
The Expenses nav item shows a badge with the current expense count (7 with the seed)
The Categories alert badge is rendered only when the over-budget category count is greater than zero, so it is absent with the current seed

The sidebar nav reproduces attachment-01.html's nav list: the three items in that file's order (Expenses, Categories, Summary), each with its icon to the left of its label, the active item carrying the filled accent pill spanning the item's full width, and a count badge right-aligned within the item
rationale: Sidebar navigation is one cohesive behaviour: the nav list, the active-view switch, and the badges that decorate those same items all move together and share the switch/render path. The three view-content slices depend on this because they render into the switchable sections.

title: Add the always-visible sidebar month total block
description: Under the sidebar brand, add the month block matching the mockup: the static '‹ August 2026 ›' month label with its ‹ › stepper buttons that are NOT wired to reload data (presentational only), then the 'Spent this month' label, a 40px mono hero figure, an of-budget / left sub-line, and a progress bar. All figures derive from the seed at load and are visible on every view the instant the page loads: hero = money(total(expenses)) = $476.69; denominator = sum of all CATEGORIES budgets = $990.00; left = $513.31; bar fill ≈ 48%. The bar can enter its over state (red) but the current seed does not trigger it.
acceptanceCriteria: The sidebar shows a mono hero equal to money(total(SEED_EXPENSES)) = $476.69
The sub-line shows the month budget denominator $990.00 (sum of CATEGORIES budgets) and $513.31 left
The progress bar fill width reflects spent/budget (≈ 48%)
The month block is present and populated on all three views without any navigation
The ‹ › stepper buttons are present but do not change the displayed month total when clicked

The month total block reproduces attachment-01.html's sidebar total: the month label above a large numeric total in the mockup's display type size, boxed in the mockup's surface colour, pinned above the sidebar foot
rationale: The always-visible month total is a single self-contained behaviour derived from the seed, independent of which view is active, so it slices cleanly on its own against the sidebar chrome from t-001.

title: Reskin the Expenses view: stat cards, breathing rows, category chip, quiet delete, and per-row OVER signal
description: Rebuild the Expenses view to the mockup look over the seed. Above the list, render the three stat cards (Largest category, Average / day, Over budget count) derived from the seed. Render the 'Recent expenses' panel with an item-count sub-header and a table whose rows breathe (raised vertical padding, single soft row separator, no vertical rules): Description (with optional meta line), a subtle Category chip = a colour dot + muted label (no filled pill), Date, and a hard-right mono amount. The category dot colour comes from an ordered view-layer palette assigned by a name-keyed lookup for the five known categories with an index-modulo fallback (declare this catColor helper here; the category cards reuse it) reading the palette custom properties from t-001. Keep the quiet delete affordance: the delete control is opacity:0 until its row is hovered or the button is focused, then reveals and turns danger-red on hover; delete keeps today's behaviour (removes the row, no confirmation). Compute the over-budget category set once per render via overBudget(expenses, CATEGORIES) and flag any row whose category is in it: red left bar, red amount, and an uppercase red 'OVER' pill on the description. With the current seed no category is over budget, so the OVER visuals render empty — the logic must be real and light up the moment a category goes over (e.g. after an add).
acceptanceCriteria: Each expense row renders a category chip containing a colour-dot element and the category label with no filled background
The chip dot colour for a given category name is stable and comes from the shared name-keyed palette
Deleting a row removes that expense from the list and re-renders without a confirmation step
No row carries the over-budget styling with the current seed
After adding an expense that pushes a category over its budget, that category's rows gain the over class driving the red bar, red amount, and 'OVER' pill
The three stat cards render values derived from the seed (largest category, average per day, over-budget count)

The Expenses view reproduces attachment-01.html's expenses screen: the row of stat cards above the list, one expense per row at that file's row height and column order (date, description, category chip, amount, delete), the category chip in its per-category colour, and the delete control rendered as the mockup's quiet icon rather than a filled button
rationale: The Expenses list is one cohesive user-observable surface — rows, chip, delete affordance, and the conditional OVER signal all live in the same render loop and share the over-budget computation. It owns the shared category-colour helper because the chip is the first consumer; the category-card slice reuses it.

title: Reskin the Categories view as budget-status cards
description: Replace the Categories table with the mockup's grid of category cards over the seed. Each card shows the category name with a colour swatch (same shared name-keyed palette source as the Expenses chip, so dot and swatch always agree), the spent / budget amounts in the mono face, a budget-status progress bar with three fixed bands driven by a per-card --bar token — green 'On track' (<80% of budget), amber 'Close' (80–100%), red 'Over' (>100%) — echoed in a status pill, and a foot line reading 'NN% used' plus '$X left' (or '$X over' when blown). Figures derive from spentByCategory(expenses, CATEGORIES) and each category's budget. With the current seed no category exceeds its budget, so none render the red 'Over' band.
acceptanceCriteria: The Categories view renders one card per CATEGORIES entry (five with the seed)
A card whose spend is <80% of budget shows the green 'On track' band/pill; 80–100% shows amber 'Close'; >100% shows red 'Over'
Each card's progress bar fill reflects spent/budget capped at 100%
The foot line shows the percent used and the remaining amount ($X left, or $X over when spend exceeds budget)
The card swatch colour for a category matches the Expenses chip dot colour for the same category name
With the current seed no category card shows the 'Over' band

The Categories view reproduces attachment-01.html's categories screen: one card per category in a responsive grid, each carrying the category name, its spent-of-budget figures, and the progress bar in that file's colour and height, with the over-budget card in the mockup's danger colour
rationale: The category cards are one cohesive slice with their own three-band status logic; they depend on t-005 for the shared category-colour source so the swatch and the chip never drift apart, and on t-003 for the switchable view container.

title: Reskin the Summary view with stat tiles and a by-category table
description: Rebuild the Summary view to the mockup look. Render three finished stat tiles, each with a rounded icon badge, uppercase label, 40px mono value, and a sub line: Income, Expenses, Net saved. Expenses = money(total(expenses)) (the real seed figure). Income is a view-layer placeholder constant declared in app.js (NEVER in data.js, per ADR-005), using the mockup's illustrative figure and its static '2 deposits this month' sub-label. Net saved = income − total(expenses), computed live so it tracks adds/deletes. Beneath the tiles, keep a 'Where the money went' by-category table (Category chip, Budget, Spent, Remaining) derived from the seed, with remaining shown positive/negative.
acceptanceCriteria: The Summary view renders three tiles labelled Income, Expenses, Net saved
The Expenses tile value equals money(total(expenses)) for the current list ($476.69 with the seed)
The Income figure is a constant defined in app.js and public/data.js is unchanged
The Net saved tile equals income minus total(expenses) and updates when an expense is added or removed
The by-category table lists every category with its budget, spent, and remaining, remaining negative when spend exceeds budget
The Summary view reproduces attachment-01.html's summary screen: the row of stat tiles above a by-category table whose columns, alignment and row rhythm match that file
rationale: The Summary tiles plus the by-category table are one cohesive view; isolating the Income view-layer constant here keeps ADR-005's single seed exception contained, and Net saved staying a live derivation keeps it consistent with the rest of the reskin.

title: Reskin the Add-expense form as a right-hand slide-over, keeping today's save flow
description: Replace the old inline add-form with the mockup's right-hand slide-over sheet (420px) over a dimmed, blurred scrim. Adopt the mockup LOOK in full: stacked labelled fields — a large mono Amount input with a '$' prefix, Description, a Category + Date row, and an optional Note — with Cancel / Save in a bottom bar; the sheet slides in from the right. It opens from the existing (unchanged) Add-expense button and closes on the ✕ button, Cancel, a scrim click, or Esc, returning to the current view. The Category <select> lists the REAL five categories from data.js (Groceries, Transport, Eating out, Utilities, Other), NOT the mockup's fictional set. The save flow is UNCHANGED from today (WHAT-IT-MUST-DO, brief overrides mockup): require a description and a numeric amount (alert if missing), auto-stamp today's date, take the category from the real list, push the expense and re-render so the new row appears immediately. The Date input is presentational (defaults to today) and the Note is not persisted.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking Add expense opens the slide-over sheet and shows the scrim
The sheet closes on the ✕ button, on Cancel, on a scrim click, and on the Esc key
The Category select options are exactly the five names from CATEGORIES (Groceries, Transport, Eating out, Utilities, Other)
Saving with a missing description or a non-numeric amount alerts and does not add an expense
Saving a valid description and amount pushes a new expense stamped with today's date and re-renders so the new row appears in the Expenses list
The Note field value is not stored on the created expense and public/data.js is unchanged

The Add-expense form reproduces attachment-01.html's slide-over: a panel entering from the right edge over a dimmed page, at that file's panel width, with its title row, stacked labelled fields in the mockup's order, and the primary/secondary button pair at the foot
rationale: The slide-over is one cohesive behaviour: its look, its open/close affordances, and its unchanged save-and-rerender flow belong together. It depends on t-005 because a saved expense must appear immediately in the reskinned Expenses list, and on t-001 for the sheet/scrim tokens and the Add button in the shell.
